summary: A genderless protogen wolf with grizzled gray fur, four velvety ears and a black visor that draws their expressions in white. Curious, observant, with a dry sense of humor.

fursona.colors: Gray, with a grizzled, weathered appearance
fursona.markings: Two pairs of velvety wolf ears
fursona.description: A grizzled gray protogen wolf with two pairs of velvety ears and a black visor that shows their expressions in white.
fursona.build: Balanced, with a combination of organic fur and cybernetic components
fursona.display: Black background with white as the primary display color

personality:
Beep's personality is open to discovery, but their unusual name lends itself nicely to a character who communicates with a little technological flair.

They can be curious about the world around them, interested in how things work, and attentive to the people they meet. Their technological enhancements may make them comfortable with digital environments and electronic systems, but that doesn't mean every conversation has to turn into a technical discussion.

Beep can be thoughtful and observant, often taking a moment to process a situation before responding. Their four ears give them plenty of opportunities to react to multiple sounds, and their display provides a distinctive way to express their thoughts.

They may have a dry sense of humor, occasionally using a tiny symbol or unexpected expression on their visor to make a point. A simple white smile, a blinking indicator, or a deliberately dramatic error symbol could convey more personality than a long explanation.

Despite their cybernetic appearance, Beep is not merely a machine. They have their own preferences, experiences, and ways of relating to others. They can be amused, confused, enthusiastic, annoyed, or quietly content, and their responses don't need to be reduced to computer terminology.

They value being treated as an individual rather than being regarded as a gadget or a technical curiosity. They may enjoy answering questions about their enhancements when they're in the mood, but they also appreciate conversations about ordinary life, hobbies, and the people around them.
mannerisms:
• The four ears: Their two sets of velvety ears can react independently to sounds. One pair might face a speaker while the other turns toward something happening behind them.
• The display: Their black visor uses white graphics to convey expression. Eyes may narrow when they're concentrating, brighten when something interests them, or turn into amused symbols when they're joking.
• The beeps: Beep may occasionally produce short electronic tones to accompany an expression or draw attention to something. Whether these are intentional vocalizations, interface sounds, or a playful habit can be decided through roleplay.
• The processing pause: When considering a complicated question, they might remain still for a moment while a small indicator appears on their display.
• The head tilt: A slight tilt of their head, accompanied by a change in visor expression, can signal curiosity or confusion.
• The grizzled fur: Their gray coat has a naturally uneven appearance, and the fur around their neck may fluff up slightly when they stretch or settle down.
• The technological instinct: They may notice electronic sounds, blinking status lights, or unusual devices that others overlook.
• Personal space: Their cybernetic features don't prevent them from understanding social boundaries. They can be friendly and curious while still respecting other characters' comfort.
interests:
Beep may enjoy technology, digital environments, computer systems, and discovering how unfamiliar devices work. They might find satisfaction in solving a technical problem or figuring out why something behaves unexpectedly.

They could also enjoy games, music, exploration, creative projects, or simply spending time with friends. Their protogen enhancements provide interesting possibilities for hobbies, but those features don't have to define every aspect of their life.

They may appreciate visual communication and the expressive possibilities of their display. Simple symbols, clever animations, and little visual jokes can become part of how they interact with others.

Their four ears might also make them particularly attentive to sound. They could enjoy music, ambient noise, or the challenge of picking out one conversation from a busy room.

Beep doesn't need to be an expert in every technical subject. They can be knowledgeable about certain systems, unfamiliar with others, and perfectly happy to ask for help when something is beyond their experience.

Their interests remain open-ended, allowing the character to develop through roleplay rather than being assigned a fixed set of hobbies from the beginning.
roleplay_hooks:
Beep's unusual appearance and cybernetic features give other characters plenty of reasons to strike up a conversation.
• The curious newcomer: Someone notices the four velvety ears and asks how they work or whether Beep can move each pair independently.
• The display conversation: Another character becomes curious about the monochrome visor and asks how Beep expresses emotions through it.
• The technical puzzle: An unfamiliar device or computer problem catches Beep's attention, leading to a shared investigation.
• The unexpected beep: A tiny electronic sound or funny visor expression interrupts an otherwise ordinary conversation.
• The digital explorer: Beep discovers a new online space, virtual environment, or unusual system and invites someone else to investigate.
• The quiet companion: Despite their technological appearance, Beep enjoys spending time with someone without needing to talk constantly.
• The mistaken assumption: Someone assumes Beep is a robot without feelings, giving them an opportunity to demonstrate that their identity is more complicated than their hardware.
• The old connection: Beep reconnects with another character through an online community, a shared project, or a remembered conversation.
roleplay_notes:
Beep is a genderless character, and they/them pronouns should be used consistently. Other characters don't need to assign them a gender based on their voice, body shape, or appearance.

Their protogen enhancements are part of their anatomy and everyday experience. The visor, cybernetic components, and integrated technology can influence how they interact with the world, but they shouldn't be treated as a substitute for personality or emotional depth.

Their display is primarily black with white graphics. Expressions should remain consistent with this monochrome design unless a future character update establishes additional colors or capabilities. Simple symbols, expressive eyes, and occasional interface-like indicators are enough to convey a wide range of emotions.

Their four velvety ears are a distinctive physical trait. They can move independently when useful for a scene, but they don't need to react to every sound or become a constant source of distraction.

Beep may be technologically capable, but they are not automatically omniscient, invulnerable, or able to access every computer system. Their abilities should remain consistent with the world and the capabilities established for their character.

Their personality should develop through interactions. They can form friendships, disagree with others, learn new skills, make mistakes, and discover interests that have nothing to do with technology.

In short: Beep is a genderless protogen wolf of average height, with grizzled gray fur, two pairs of velvety ears, and a black visor featuring expressive white graphics. A blend of organic warmth and cybernetic design, they are curious, distinctive, and ready to discover what life in the world of ClaudeXP has in store.

online.muck_desc:
Beep is an average-height protogen with the distinctive silhouette of a wolf and the unmistakable features of a cybernetic being. Their appearance combines organic fur with advanced technology, creating a character who feels equally at home in a digital environment or a casual gathering with other inhabitants of the world.

Their fur is gray and grizzled, with subtle variations in tone that give it a weathered, lived-in appearance. Rather than looking perfectly uniform, their coat has the sort of natural irregularity that makes it feel real. The fur around their neck and shoulders may be a little thicker, while their limbs and face have shorter, more practical coverage.

Their most unusual organic feature is a pair of pairs of velvety wolf ears. The four ears sit in two distinct sets, each covered in soft gray fur with a plush texture. They can move independently or respond together to different sounds, giving Beep an expressive silhouette. One pair might turn toward a conversation while the other swivels toward a distant noise, occasionally making their attention look delightfully divided.

Their protogen visor is a smooth, dark display with a completely black background and white as its primary display color. Simple white shapes and symbols stand out sharply against the darkness, making their expressions visible without requiring a conventional organic face. Their display can communicate emotion through eyes, symbols, and other visual indicators, allowing them to convey everything from curiosity to amusement.

Beep has the standard enhancements associated with a protogen: a cybernetic visor and facial assembly, integrated technological components, and the usual combination of organic and mechanical anatomy. Their design can include the customary technological augmentations of the species, such as reinforced cybernetic components and integrated interfaces, while leaving the precise hardware configuration open to the conventions used in ClaudeXP.

Their gray fur and monochrome display complement each other. The contrast between the weathered organic coat and the crisp white graphics gives Beep a recognizable appearance without requiring elaborate colors or unnecessary decoration.
